name: Unused app permission reset
plain: Automatically removes permissions from apps not opened for months.
meaning: Limits dormant exposure. Android resets runtime permissions after about three months unused; iOS has no automatic revocation.

android.persistence: Resets after a few months unused; app hibernates
android.note: Applies to apps targeting API 30 and later by default; backported to 6.0 via Play services in 2021-22.

ios.note: iOS never auto-revokes; location reminders prompt periodically.

story.what_it_is: Automatically takes away permissions from apps you have not opened for months.

marketing.name: Permission auto reset
marketing.pitch: Android removes permissions from apps you have not used in a few months, and tells you.

story.for_you: If you have not opened an app for about three months, its permissions go away. You get a notice and can turn them back on. You never need to clean up old apps yourself.
story.for_makers: Dormant apps keep access forever, which is a risk. Auto reset cuts that exposure. Makers have to ask again when the person returns, so they need a good reason to win trust back.

use_cases.example: A game you played last summer loses location access and asks again when you open it.
A holiday shopping app loses camera access until you come back in winter.
A trip app that you used once loses its location permission.
A fitness app you forgot about loses health data access.
An old social app loses its contacts access.
A tracking SDK inside a stale app loses its sensor access.
A security team sees fewer old permissions across a fleet of phones.

story.android_note: Applies to apps for Android 11 and later by default, and was backported to Android 6 through Play services in 2021 and 2022.
story.ios_note: iPhone never takes permissions away on its own. It reminds you now and then about location use.

history.change: Auto-reset backported via Google Play services
